QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_1

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (Chartered Accountant SIA) has been engaged by Antyodaya Seva Sangh, an NPO listed on NSE-SSE, to conduct the Annual Impact Report assessment for FY 2024-25. The NPO runs four programmes — watershed management, women SHG training, slum housing repair and rural cataract camps — each under a different SAS standard. Under the general framework of SAS-100, what is the PRIMARY obligation of the SIA when scoping a multi-activity engagement?

answer.text: Assess only the programme with the largest rupee outlay and extrapolate findings across the others to save engagement time
Combine all four programmes under a single consolidated SAS standard selected by the Responsible Party (NPO management)
Apply the activity-specific SAS standard to each programme while ensuring the overall assessment methodology, independence and reporting conform to SAS-100
Sub-contract the non-core programmes to other SIAs and limit the engagement letter to one programme of the SIA's choice

explanation.text: The Logic: SAS-100 is the umbrella General Standard that governs every SIA engagement — it sets the rules on independence, evidence, materiality, sampling, reporting and assurance language. Where an SE runs multiple thematic activities, each activity is assessed against its own subject-matter SAS standard (200, 400, 500, 1100, 1300 etc.), but the engagement-wide governance stays with SAS-100. Option C captures this correctly. The Trap: Option A (largest-outlay only) violates SAS-100's completeness requirement. Option B surrenders SIA independence — the SIA, not the SE, selects the applicable standard. Option D shirks the engagement accepted in the letter. Cross-Exam Context: XXIII Ch 8. Related umbrella-standard logic appears in XV (Research Analyst) Chapter on research policy and in III-A (Compliance — general obligations vs product-specific rules). Assessor's Pro-Tip: When a single SE runs multi-thematic projects, build the engagement plan as a matrix — rows = programmes, columns = SAS-100 control areas (sampling %, MoV, materiality, assurance type). One plan, one opinion, multiple indicator sets.
